name: ABB
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: ABB's Electrification business is running the hottest data-center order book of any diversified electrical: Q2 2026 orders hit $7.2B (+60%, first quarter ever above $7B), data-center order growth was 'triple-digit', Americas Electrification orders rose +114%, and segment backlog swelled to $13.7B (+57%). Its differentiated AIDC weapons are HiPerGuard — the industry's first static medium-voltage UPS (2.5-25 MW, 98% efficiency, new 34.5 kV direct-grid-connect class) — and Motion's flywheel synchronous condensers, 62 of which VoltaGrid has ordered for behind-the-meter AI campuses. BACKGROUND: Under CEO Morten Wierod (since August 2024) the portfolio is being aggressively reshaped: Robotics sold to SoftBank for $5.375B (scrapping a planned spin-off), a $5.5B recommended offer for UK valve-actuator maker Rotork (ABB's biggest-ever deal, received as 'pricy' — shares fell 4%), a $2B buyback, and ~$14B of remaining M&A firepower. Context worth holding: ABB is a top-5 but not the leader in data-center power (Schneider leads; in UPS ABB ranks behind Schneider, Vertiv, Eaton, and Huawei), it sold its grid business to Hitachi before the grid supercycle, and it is a three-time US bribery settler (2004, 2010, and the 2022 $315M Kusile/Eskom FCPA resolution) — a standing counterparty-diligence flag.
ecosystemRole: We assess ABB as the AIDC power chain's medium-voltage innovator — the vendor pushing the UPS and stability functions up to MV where gigawatt campuses actually need them, while competing as a strong #2-5 across the broader data-center electrical stack. Basis: HiPerGuard is the industry's first static MV UPS and the centerpiece of NVIDIA-ecosystem 800 VDC architecture work (with SACE Infinitus, the first IEC-certified solid-state breaker); the VoltaGrid orders (62 flywheel synchronous condensers) put ABB inside the fastest-moving behind-the-meter AI power deployments; and third-party rankings place the top five (Schneider, ABB, Eaton, Vertiv, Delta) at ~41-43% of the $35B data-center power market. ~40% of ABB's electrification research is aimed at next-generation data-center technologies. Its scope overlaps Eaton and Schneider on distribution/UPS, Vertiv on critical power, and increasingly Hitachi Energy at the grid interface.

productsAndServices.name: HiPerGuard MV UPS (flagship differentiator)
productsAndServices.description: Industry's first static medium-voltage UPS: solid-state ZISC architecture (isolating line reactor + coupling transformer at MV, converters and Li-ion storage at LV). 2.5 MW per unit, hard-parallel to 25 MW; voltage classes 6-24 kV plus a new 34.5 kV class (Q2 2026) allowing direct grid connection without voltage conversion; 98% efficiency; intrusive maintenance only at 10-year intervals; microgrid-ready (integrates BESS, gas turbines, renewables; grid support and peak shaving). Designed and largely produced in Napier, New Zealand.
productsAndServices.positioning: Category-creating product — moves UPS from LV to MV, cutting conversion stages for 100 MW+ AI campuses; deployed at Applied Digital's Polaris Forge campuses in 25 MW blocks.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to hyperscalers/neoclouds/colos and via EPC partners.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Core building block of ABB's 800 VDC architecture with NVIDIA (MV UPS feeding DC distribution via solid-state power electronics).

productsAndServices.name: LV UPS, switchgear & busway
productsAndServices.description: MegaFlex DPA UPS expanded March 2026 to 1,000-2,000 kW per system (97.6% VFI efficiency, Xtra VFI adaptive modules, 15-year design life); MNS LV switchgear with Emax 3 breakers (European capacity +120% across Brno/Rakovski for hyperscale demand); MV switchgear families (Advance, SafeGear, ZX GIS to 40.5 kV, SafePlus RMU to 38 kV); ReliaGear busway to 5,000 A and metal-enclosed bus to 34.5 kV/6,000 A.
productsAndServices.positioning: Top-5 global data-center power/UPS/PDU player per MarketsandMarkets — behind Schneider (category leader) and, in UPS, also behind Vertiv, Eaton, and Huawei; North American top-5 (with Schneider, Vertiv, Eaton, Mitsubishi Electric) holding ~62% collectively.
productsAndServices.roadmap: US capacity: $110M package (Richmond VA power quality, Senatobia MS Emax 3, Pinetops NC grid components); $200M European MV expansion incl. SF6-free lines (Dalmine).

productsAndServices.name: Synchronous condensers with flywheels (Motion, High Power)
productsAndServices.description: High-inertia synchronous condensers with flywheel energy storage — instantaneous inertia ('shock absorbers for the grid'), short-circuit strength, and reactive-power voltage support for behind-the-meter AI campuses running on gensets/turbines. Delivered as integrated packages: excitation and automation in prefabricated eHouses with MV/LV panels, VFDs, and PLCs. VoltaGrid orders: 27 units (Nov 2025, first operational April 2026) + 35 more (CERAWeek, March 2026) = 62 total; a related ~$150M Motion order booked Q2 2026.
productsAndServices.positioning: The rotating-stability answer to AI load volatility — sits alongside (not inside) the BESS-buffering approach; directly relevant wherever behind-the-meter generation runs weak-grid islands.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to microgrid providers (VoltaGrid) and utilities; packaged with Automation's eHouses.
productsAndServices.roadmap: VoltaGrid partnership positions ABB in the Permian-style distributed-generation fleet model scaling across US AI campuses; unit dollar values undisclosed.

productsAndServices.name: 800 VDC / solid-state DC portfolio (NVIDIA collaboration)
productsAndServices.description: October 2025 NVIDIA collaboration on 800 VDC power for gigawatt-scale AI data centers and 1 MW racks: HiPerGuard MV UPS + high-efficiency MVAC-to-LVDC converters + SACE Infinitus (world's first IEC-certified solid-state circuit breaker) + DC switchgear/busway + storage + monitoring. June 2026 phase 2: ABB power systems integrated as SimReady 3D assets into NVIDIA's Omniverse DSX blueprint for source-to-rack digital-twin power design.
productsAndServices.positioning: Puts ABB in the same NVIDIA 800 VDC ecosystem as Vertiv, Eaton, Delta, and Hitachi Energy; ABB's edge is the MV UPS + certified solid-state breaker combination. Claimed DC benefits: up to 20% better conductor utilization, reduced copper use.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: NVIDIA ecosystem co-design; direct to AI-factory developers.
productsAndServices.roadmap: White-paper architecture (Purgat/Strassel; ODCA board seat) positions ABB for the 2027+ 800 VDC rack transition.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q2 2026: record orders $12.0B (+30%); Electrification orders $7.2B (+60%) with triple-digit data-center growth; $5.5B Rotork offer announced — shares fell 4%
recentDevelopments.read: The operational story (Op. EBITA beat, backlog +27%, guidance raised to low-double-digit-to-low-teens growth) was overshadowed by deal-price concerns: analysts called Rotork 'pricy' and RBC floated counter-bid risk. GAAP EPS missed (~$0.66 vs ~$0.74) on discontinued-ops noise. Management insists the DC surge is 'real customer investment, not pre-buying' — while conceding quarterly lumpiness.

recentDevelopments.headline: NVIDIA phase 2: ABB power systems integrated as SimReady 3D assets into the Omniverse DSX blueprint
recentDevelopments.read: Digital-twin power design from source to rack — AI factories will be electrically designed in simulation with ABB equipment as native building blocks. A subtle but sticky form of design-in lock: specification wins happen in the twin before procurement opens.

recentDevelopments.headline: $200M European MV investment over 3 years: Dalmine SF6-free AIS plus GIS/vacuum-interrupter/relay capacity across five countries
recentDevelopments.read: Follows the +120% European LV switchgear expansion (Brno/Rakovski) and the $110M US package — ABB's capacity response is broad-based but smaller-ticket than Hitachi's or Siemens Energy's transformer programs, consistent with its distribution-not-transmission scope.

recentDevelopments.headline: VoltaGrid extension at CERAWeek: 35 more flywheel synchronous condensers + eHouses (62 units total across both orders)
recentDevelopments.read: Independently verified by trade press, dollar value undisclosed. VoltaGrid's distributed-generation fleet model (validated by the 900 MW Vantage/OpenAI campus win) makes ABB's rotating stability hardware a de facto standard in behind-the-meter AI power — the clearest evidence that AI load volatility is creating a new product category.

recentDevelopments.headline: MegaFlex DPA UPS range expanded to 1,000-2,000 kW targeting hyperscale, colocation, and 'neocloud'
recentDevelopments.read: The LV complement to HiPerGuard — ABB explicitly naming neoclouds as a segment confirms where the incremental UPS demand is. Q2 2026 also introduced the 34.5 kV HiPerGuard class for direct grid connection.

recentDevelopments.headline: Up to $2B share buyback launched through January 2027; CFO transition to Christian Nilsson (ex-Electrification CFO) effective February 1
recentDevelopments.read: Capital returns continue alongside the M&A program. FY2025 closed as a record year: orders $36.8B (+17%), Op. EBITA margin 19.0% (all-time high), Q4 the first quarter ever above $10B orders with ~$600M of individual >$100M data-center orders.

recentDevelopments.headline: Applied Digital Polaris Forge 2 (Harwood, ND): HiPerGuard MV UPS + MV/LV switchgear for 300 MW, scaling in 25 MW blocks
recentDevelopments.read: The reference deployment for MV-UPS architecture at neocloud scale — initial 200 MW leased to a US hyperscaler. Extends the June 2025 Polaris Forge 1 (400 MW) collaboration; ABB is becoming the electrical standard for Applied Digital's buildout.

recentDevelopments.headline: NVIDIA collaboration on 800 VDC power for gigawatt AI factories: HiPerGuard + SACE Infinitus solid-state breaker
recentDevelopments.read: ABB's entry ticket to the 1 MW rack era. Its 800 VDC white paper (~40% of electrification research now aimed at next-gen DC technologies) stakes the claim that the MV UPS + solid-state DC distribution chain is the winning architecture.

recentDevelopments.headline: Robotics divested to SoftBank for $5.375B — spin-off plan scrapped; ~$5.3B net cash funds the M&A pivot
recentDevelopments.read: Wierod's defining portfolio move: exit a #2-global robotics franchise ('limited synergies') to double down on electrification and automation. The proceeds are already committed — ~$4.8B toward Rotork — with ~$14B of stated remaining firepower that the press flags as an 'M&A-risk discount' on the multiple.

strategyRead: (High confidence) ABB is winning the medium-voltage layer of AI power: HiPerGuard has no direct static-MV-UPS competitor at scale, the 34.5 kV class removes a conversion stage entirely, and reference deployments (Applied Digital, 25 MW blocks) plus the NVIDIA 800 VDC role make it the architecture incumbent for the next rack generation. Basis: company-published product specs and deployment announcements, corroborated by trade press; the 'no direct competitor' read is ours — Eaton/Schneider/Vertiv compete at LV.

(High confidence) The VoltaGrid synchronous-condenser franchise (62 units) is the strongest independent validation that AI load volatility — the problem Hitachi's CEO warned about and Bloomberg confirmed is damaging equipment — is now a purchasable product category. ABB's flywheel-condenser-plus-eHouse package is the de facto standard in US behind-the-meter AI microgrids. Basis: two verified orders across two years; dollar values undisclosed, so revenue materiality is unproven.

(Moderate confidence) ABB is a strong top-5, not the leader: Schneider leads data-center power overall, and in UPS ABB trails Schneider, Vertiv, Eaton, and Huawei. Its bet is that the MV/800 VDC transition resets the leaderboard in its favor — plausible but unproven, since hyperscaler electrical architectures change slowly and Vertiv/Eaton have deeper US hyperscale UPS incumbency. Basis: MarketsandMarkets/Mordor rankings; the reset thesis is our inference.

(Moderate confidence) Capital allocation is now the biggest swing factor in the equity story: Robotics proceeds recycled into Rotork at a price the market disliked, ~$14B of stated firepower creating deal-risk overhang, consensus Neutral with the average target below spot, P/E ~37. Operationally excellent, fully priced, and one more expensive deal from a de-rating. Basis: third-party analyst coverage and share-price reactions.

(High confidence) Two structural facts warrant standing awareness in any counterparty relationship: ABB sold its grid/transmission business to Hitachi before the supercycle (its AIDC story is distribution-side only — it cannot supply the transformers and HVDC its campuses' grid connections need), and it is a three-time US bribery settler (2004, 2010, 2022 Kusile/$315M) — procurement and compliance teams at large customers know this history. Basis: DOJ resolution documents and deal record.
